newsitem.title: USA: US average retail beef prices sink in January - NCBA.
newsitem.headline: US average retail beef prices sink in January - NCBA.

text.p: Average retail beef prices were down in January from December with the average price for 15 beef cuts averaging $2.39 per lb versus $2.59 in December, the National Cattlemen's Beef Association (NCBA) said in a report.

The January price report, released Thursday, is the first since the NCBA changed its survey to include 15 cuts of beef from the previous six. Also included in the survey were special low advertised beef prices, prices for all grades of beef and prices gathered throughout the month rather than once a month.
The survey area was divided into five geographic areas and includes all states except Alaska and Hawaii versus the previous 19-city survey.

NCBA said January beef prices were relatively low because beef production was seasonally large. Using year-ago price data from Cattle-Fax, a market research firm, NCBA said the January average of $2.39 compares with $2.40 a year ago.

The averages of the five regions for the 15 cuts in January were ground chuck $1.56 per lb, regular ground beef $1.27, lean ground beef $2.13, select boneless chuck roast $1.75, choice boneless chuck roast $1.77, choice boneless round roast $2.15, select round roast $2.19, choice rib roast $3.99, choice T-bone steak $4.75, choice rib-eye steak $5.76, choice boneless round steak $2.21, select round steak $2.02, select sirloin steak $2.99, choice boneless sirloin steak $2.94, and boneless beef for stew $2.24.
